Employee Remote-Work Policy

Organisation: [Company Name]  |  Policy Owner: Human Resources  |  Version: 1.0  |  Effective Date: [DD Month YYYY]  |  Next Review: [Date, 12 months after effective date]

1. Purpose

This policy sets out the conditions under which employees may work remotely. It aims to give employees flexibility while protecting company information, maintaining service quality, keeping working arrangements fair and consistent, and meeting the company's legal and health-and-safety obligations.

2. Scope

This policy applies to all employees of [Company Name] (“the Company”) who have been approved to work remotely, in whole or in part, under this policy. It applies to full-time, part-time and fixed-term employees. It does not apply to contractors, agency workers or interns, who are governed by their own agreements, unless those agreements expressly refer to this policy.

This policy does not change an employee's contractual terms, hours of work, pay or entitlements. Where a local law or collective agreement provides more favourable terms, those terms prevail.

3. Definitions

TermMeaning
Remote WorkPerforming contracted duties from an approved location other than the Company's office, such as an employee's home.
Hybrid WorkA working arrangement that combines remote work with time spent at a Company office.
Approved WorkspaceThe primary location, meeting the requirements of Section 6, from which the employee is authorised to work remotely.
Core HoursThe daily window during which remote employees must be available for meetings and collaboration, as set by their manager.
Company EquipmentHardware, software and accessories owned, leased or licensed by the Company and issued to the employee.
Company InformationAll data, documents, communications and systems belonging to or held on behalf of the Company, including personal data of employees and customers.
ManagerThe employee's line manager or any other person formally designated to approve remote-work arrangements.
Remote-Work AgreementThe written record of an employee's approved remote-work arrangement, signed by the employee and manager.

4. Eligibility

  1. Eligibility criteria. An employee may be considered for remote work where all of the following apply:
    1. they have completed their probationary period, or their manager has approved an exception in writing;
    2. their role's duties can be performed remotely without material loss of quality, productivity or customer service;
    3. they have a performance rating of “meets expectations” or higher in their most recent review cycle;
    4. they have an Approved Workspace that meets Section 6; and
    5. they can meet the Core Hours and communication expectations in Section 5.
  2. Roles that require on-site presence. Roles requiring physical presence (for example, certain laboratory, warehouse, facilities, reception or hands-on technical roles) are not eligible for fully remote work. Hybrid arrangements may still be possible where the role permits.
  3. Approval. Remote work requires written approval from the employee's manager and HR, recorded in a signed Remote-Work Agreement before the arrangement begins.
  4. Discretion. Approval is at the Company's discretion, based on business needs. Eligibility is reviewed at least annually and whenever the employee's role or circumstances change.

5. Policy Requirements

  1. Working hours and availability
    1. Remote employees shall work their contracted hours and record time in the Company's timekeeping system.
    2. Employees shall be available during Core Hours, as set by their manager, for meetings, calls and collaboration.
    3. Any change to usual working hours requires prior approval from the manager.
  2. Communication
    1. Employees shall keep their status current in the Company's messaging platform during working hours.
    2. Responses to internal messages shall follow the response-time standards set by the team, and urgent matters shall be escalated by phone.
    3. Employees shall attend scheduled team meetings in person or by video, with cameras on where practical and agreed with the team.
  3. Location of work
    1. Employees shall work only from the Approved Workspace, unless the manager has approved another location in advance.
    2. Employees working from another country require prior written approval from HR, as this may create tax, employment-law, immigration and data-protection obligations.
    3. Employees shall not work while travelling in a vehicle or in public places where Company Information could be overheard or viewed.
  4. Workplace health and safety
    1. Employees shall maintain a safe workspace, free from trip hazards, with adequate lighting, ventilation and a suitable chair and desk.
    2. Employees shall complete the Company's remote-work self-assessment on joining and annually thereafter.
    3. Employees shall report any work-related injury or illness, including those occurring at home, to their manager within 24 hours.
    4. The Company may, on reasonable notice and with the employee's consent, arrange a virtual or in-person workspace assessment.
  5. Expenses and reimbursement
    1. Employees are responsible for their own home internet and utility costs unless otherwise agreed in writing.
    2. Work-related expenses pre-approved under the Company's expense policy are reimbursable on submission of receipts.
  6. Attendance at the office
    1. Remote employees may be required to attend the office for meetings, training, onboarding or other business needs, with at least [5] working days' notice where practicable.
    2. Reasonable travel expenses for required office attendance are reimbursed in line with the Company's expense policy.
  7. Changes to or withdrawal of arrangements
    1. Remote-work arrangements may be modified or withdrawn by the Company where business needs, performance or policy compliance require it. The Company shall give at least [30] days' written notice, except where a security or conduct issue requires immediate action.
    2. Employees may request a change to their arrangement at any time through their manager.

6. Equipment Requirements

  1. Company-issued equipment
    1. The Company will issue a laptop, monitor(s), headset and any other essential equipment for the employee's role, as determined by IT.
    2. Company Equipment remains the property of the Company, must be used primarily for business purposes, and must be returned on request or on leaving the Company.
    3. Employees shall not lend, sell or permit others, including family members, to use Company Equipment.
  2. Personal devices
    1. Personal devices may be used to access Company systems only where they are enrolled in the Company's mobile device management (MDM) platform and meet the minimum standards set by IT.
    2. Personal devices must not store Company Information outside approved applications.
  3. Approved Workspace standards
    1. The workspace must provide a private area where calls and confidential material cannot be overheard or viewed by others.
    2. The employee must have a reliable broadband connection with a minimum download speed of [25] Mbps and upload speed of [5] Mbps.
    3. The employee must have a backup connection option, such as a mobile hotspot, for use if the primary connection fails.
  4. Support and maintenance
    1. IT will provide remote support for Company Equipment. Hardware faults must be reported to IT within one working day.
    2. Employees shall install software updates and security patches promptly when prompted by the Company's systems.

7. Information Security Requirements

  1. Access and authentication
    1. Employees shall access Company systems only through approved methods, such as the Company VPN or zero-trust access platform.
    2. Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is mandatory for all Company accounts.
    3. Passwords must be unique and managed through the Company-approved password manager. Passwords and MFA codes must never be shared.
  2. Data handling
    1. Company Information must be stored only in approved Company systems. Local storage on devices is prohibited unless encrypted and approved by IT.
    2. Printing of Company Information at home is prohibited unless the manager has approved it. Any approved printed material must be locked away when not in use and shredded when no longer needed.
    3. Personal email, personal cloud storage and personal messaging applications must not be used for Company business.
  3. Device security
    1. Full-disk encryption must be enabled on all devices used for Company work.
    2. Devices must lock automatically after no more than [10] minutes of inactivity and must be locked whenever the employee steps away.
    3. Antivirus and endpoint protection must remain active at all times.
  4. Household and third parties
    1. Employees shall ensure that family members, visitors and others cannot access Company devices or Company Information.
    2. Smart speakers and other voice-activated devices must be switched off or moved out of the room during confidential calls.
  5. Incident reporting
    1. Lost or stolen devices, suspected phishing, malware, or any suspected data breach must be reported to the IT Service Desk immediately and in any event within one hour of discovery.
    2. Employees must cooperate fully with any investigation of a security incident.

8. Responsibilities

RoleKey responsibilities
EmployeeFollow this policy; maintain an Approved Workspace; be available during Core Hours; protect Company Information and Equipment; report incidents and injuries promptly; complete the annual self-assessment.
ManagerAssess requests against eligibility criteria; agree Core Hours and output expectations; maintain the Remote-Work Agreement; monitor performance and wellbeing; approve exceptions; give notice of changes.
Human ResourcesOwn this policy and its review; co-approve Remote-Work Agreements; advise on cross-border work, working-time and health-and-safety matters; manage the expense and attendance-notice process.
IT DepartmentProvision and support Company Equipment; enforce MFA, encryption and MDM; maintain VPN and secure access platforms; run the IT Service Desk and incident response.
Information SecuritySet security standards for remote work; investigate incidents; audit compliance with Section 7; advise on data-protection obligations.
Facilities / Health & SafetyProvide guidance on home-workspace ergonomics and safety; support workspace assessments; record and review reported incidents.
FinanceProcess approved expense claims and reimbursements in line with the expense policy.

9. Non-Compliance and Review

  1. Non-compliance
    1. Breach of this policy may result in withdrawal of remote-work privileges and, where serious or repeated, disciplinary action under the Company's disciplinary policy.
    2. Breaches of Section 7 (Information Security) may also result in access being suspended pending investigation.
  2. Questions and disputes
    1. Questions about this policy should be directed to the employee's manager or HR.
    2. Employees who disagree with a decision about their remote-work arrangement may raise a grievance under the Company's grievance procedure.
  3. Review
    1. HR will review this policy at least every 12 months, and earlier if legislation, business needs or security risks change.
